title: Nilang .nilax manifest, format_version 1
description: The manifest a `nil build` produces today. This schema documents the format as implemented rather than the format the ecosystem would prefer; the preferred field set is manifest-v2.schema.json, which is proposed, not implemented.
known_gaps: There is no source_revision, so a package does not identify the source it was built from.
There is no runtime_abi, so a package cannot state which runtime it needs.
There is no payload_checksums, so per-file integrity depends entirely on the whole-archive signature being checked by a verifier that already knows the expected digest.
signature is a bare string here, while pkg/signing.PackageSignature is a structured object. Two representations of one fact is the defect manifest-v2 removes.
There is no app_id distinct from app_name; the store uses a reverse-DNS name in app_name, which works but is not typed.

format_version.description: Manifest format version. Only 1 is a stable format.

app_name.description: Application identity. In the ecosystem this carries a reverse-DNS id such as org.onuron.calculator.

entry_bytecode.description: Archive-relative path of the entry bytecode. Must resolve to a file present in the archive.

targets.description: Targets the package is built for. Every entry must appear in abi/runtime-abi.json; an unknown target is refused, never assumed future-proof.

created_at.description: Build timestamp, RFC 3339. Pinned from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-equivalent input when the build is reproducible, so two builds of identical inputs are byte-identical.

compiler_version.description: Version of the NilLang compiler that produced the package.

dependencies.description: Declared dependencies, name to version constraint.

permissions.description: Requested capabilities. Despite the name this is the capability set; it is the mirror of nil.json's `capabilities`. Every entry must appear in capabilities/vocabulary.json.

metadata.description: Free-form string metadata. Not security relevant and not covered by any signature rule today.

signature.description: Whole-archive signature. Present only on a signed build; an unsigned package is not invalid by schema but is refused by a verifier that requires trust. See signing/signing.json.

target.description: A target identifier declared in abi/runtime-abi.json under `targets`.
